description: Rescales the LEVELS inside a mixfile, writing a new mixfile (text -> text, a DATA output): every level in lines startline..endline is multiplied by gain and written back as a 4-decimal linear value. dB-notated levels are CONVERTED to linear in the process (verified: '-6dB' at gain 0.5 -> '0.2506'), pan columns pass through untouched, comment lines are STRIPPED from the output, and times/names are preserved. gain above 1 amplifies (3.0 verified: levels 1.0/0.8 -> 3.0000/2.4000 - 'attenuate' is a misnomer, it is a level multiplier). The line-range flags make it a group fader: '-s2 -e2' rescaled only line 2, leaving line 1 bit-unchanged (verified). Output verified round-trip: submix mix accepts the rewritten file directly. Takes no audio inputs (arity 0, mixfile as pre-output aux). Deterministic.
musical_use: The getlevel companion and the mixfile group-fader: when 'submix getlevel 3' reports a NORMALISATION REQUIRED factor below 1 you can either pass it as submix mix's atten (one render) or bake it permanently into the mixfile here (better when the mixfile will be reused, shuffled, or extended - the corrected levels travel with the file). The startline/endline range turns it into a stem fader: attenuate just the pile-up region getlevel pinpointed, duck lines 5-12 while leaving the bed alone, or push a group up with gain > 1. Also the clean way to NORMALISE NOTATION: a pass at gain 1.0 converts all dB levels to plain multipliers - do this before submix pan, whose dB handling is broken (see that entry).

inmixfile.description: The mixfile to rescale (write it with write_data_file(); standard mixfile syntax - levels as multipliers or dB forms, optional pans, ';' comments). Renders in the argv BEFORE the output path. The named sound files must exist (CDP validates them - cwd-relative paths as in submix mix).

gain.description: REQUIRED level multiplier applied to every level in range (values > 1 amplify; banner says 'must be > 0.0' but CDP ACCEPTS 0, writing all-zero levels = a silent mix downstream - curated minimum keeps it positive; -1 and 40000 refused '(0.000000 to 32767.000000)' verbatim). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.').

startline.description: First mixfile line to rescale (1-based, counting sound lines; default: first). CDP-enforced 1 to the file's line count (input-dependent: '-s0' on a 2-line file refused 'Parameter[2] Value (0.000000) out of range (1.000000 to 2.000000)' verbatim). Omitted unless set.

endline.description: Last mixfile line to rescale (default: last; same input-dependent 1-to-linecount bound). Set equal to startline to touch a single line (verified). Omitted unless set.

examples.description: Bake getlevel's correction factor into the mixfile.
examples.expected_use: Run submix getlevel 3 first; its NORMALISATION REQUIRED factor (when < 1) is the gain. The rewritten mixfile then renders clean through submix mix at default atten.

examples.description: Duck only the middle events of a mix.
examples.expected_use: Lines 3-6 halved, everything else byte-preserved. Feed the output path to submix mix's mixfile parameter as graphs/<graph_id>/<name>.txt.

known_issues: The output is a DATA file (a rewritten mixfile, .txt): not audio - its consumer is submix mix's (or another mixfile entry's) aux parameter, referenced by session-relative path. The duration pre-flight is skipped (duration_model 'static' is a placeholder).

COMMENTS ARE STRIPPED and formatting is normalised in the output (levels rewritten as 4-decimal linear values; ';' lines dropped - verified). Keep annotated master mixfiles separate if you care about the comments.

dB level notation is CONVERTED to linear on the way through (verified '-6dB' -> 0.2506 at gain 0.5). This is the sanctioned dB-to-linear converter for the family - run gain 1.0 before submix pan (whose own dB handling corrupts levels).

gain 0 is CDP-legal but writes an all-zero-level mixfile that renders silence downstream (curated minimum 0.000001 keeps it reachable-but-nonzero). Values > 1 amplify - re-run getlevel afterwards if you push levels up.

The named sound files must exist and be valid (CDP parses the mixfile fully; missing names refuse with the 'is not a sndfile' warning family). Line numbers are 1-based and bounds are input-dependent (refusals quote the file's own line count).
Deterministic: byte-identical output run to run. gain refuses breakpoints (parameter 1).
Arity-0 entry: call process() with no input argument. Data output - duration_row null in the findings.
